raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fix a `NixlPushConnector` hang in 2P2D EP16.

The model thread was calling NIXL for heartbeats and outgoing WRITE completion polling. If one rank blocked in either call, it missed the next expert-parallel collective and the request timed out.

This change is required by the 2P2D EP16 write step in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62007.

## Changes

- Move push heartbeat processing to `nixl-push-writer`.
- Move outgoing WRITE completion polling to `nixl-push-writer`.
- Return completed and failed request IDs to the model thread through a queue.
- Keep WRITE completion and failure accounting under the transfer lock.
- Serialize writer NIXL calls with handshake setup.
- Add unit coverage for thread ownership and WRITE completion accounting.

The change is limited to `NixlPushConnector`.

## Test plan

Set the UCX environment on all four nodes:

```bash
export UCX_TLS=rc_verbs,ud_verbs,tcp,self,rocm
export UCX_NET_DEVICES=ionic_0:1,lo
export UCX_IB_GID_INDEX=1
export UCX_UD_VERBS_ETH_DGID_CHECK=n
export UCX_IB_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA=yes
export UCX_RMA_PPLN_ENABLE=y
export UCX_PROTO_EMULATION_ENABLE=n
```

Use this KV configuration on prefill:

```bash
KV='{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"backends":["UCX"],"kv_lease_duration":180}}'
```

Use the same configuration on decode with `"kv_role":"kv_consumer"`.

Start the prefill master:

```bash
vllm serve DeepSeek-V3 --port 20005 -tp 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 8 \
  --data-parallel-address $PREFILL_MASTER --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 \
  --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend mori_high_throughput \
  --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --api-server-count 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.75 --kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

Start the second prefill node with the same command and:

```bash
--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 8
```

Start the decode master with the prefill command adjusted to:

```bash
--data-parallel-address $DECODE_MASTER \
--all2all-backend mori_low_latency \
--kv-transfer-config "$KV"
```

Remove `--enforce-eager` on decode. Start the second decode node with `--headless --data-parallel-start-rank 8`.

Start the router:

```bash
vllm-router --vllm-pd-disaggregation --kv-connector nixl \
  --prefill http://$PREFILL_MASTER:20005 \
  --decode http://$DECODE_MASTER:20005 \
  --worker-startup-timeout-secs 7200 --port 30000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --intra-node-data-parallel-size 8 --policy round_robin \
  --prefill-policy round_robin --decode-policy round_robin
```

Run GSM8K:

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k \
  --model_args model=DeepSeek-V3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=1,tokenized_requests=False,trust_remote_code=True
```

Run static checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/push_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

## Results

2P2D EP16/DP16 completed with GSM8K exact_match `0.96`.

Regression runs also completed:

- 1P1D TP8: `0.96`
- 1P1D EP8/DP8: `0.92`

All runs used GPU-direct `rc_verbs/ionic_0` for inter-node KV WRITE.

nodes.body:
Thanks for the update!

I see your point, yet I'd drop the 1 ms polling. As I understand it, it doesn't solve what you are trying to solve.

Even if the writer polls every ms, the model thread only picks up the results once per engine step. So the thread can poll as much as it wants. It has no effect until the engine finishes its step.

Do you maybe have a profile of the rank that blocked?
I suspect P sends no heartbeats because `heartbeat_by_engine` is only filled on D. And `check_xfer_state` has no blocking wait in NIXL.

@YannikHinteregger you were right about the 1 ms poll. On cebf114 the writer only uses that wait while a PUSH_REG is still unmatched. In-flight writes just wake with the engine step, and check_xfer_state does not hold the lock. The handshake lock only covers the two agent setup calls, and the heartbeat map is copied before it is queued. I also removed the receive override.
@YannikHinteregger any suggestions , or can you help merge

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the contribution. While testing something unrelated, I ran into the same delay. I retested with your branch. Your polling mechanism reduced the delay under some loads. That led me to the root cause in NIXL. I opened ai-dynamo/nixl#2441 to fix it.

In my tests the polling helped most at medium load. At high load the delay was still clearly there, probably because the polling thread competes with the engine for CPU time.

So I suggest we drop the polling from this PR and wait for the NIXL fix to land. The rest of the change looks reasonable to me.

Could you also take a look at the broken tests?
A test for the hang itself would also be great. Thanks
The model thread takes this lock too, so couldn't a blocking NIXL call here still cause the hang?

nodes.body: This also removes main's 1 ms self-poll, which the writer ran while P held finished blocks with no matching PUSH_REG (added with the push connector in #35264). If a PUSH_REG reaches P after the prefill has finished (for example, D queued the request), P now drains it only on its next get_transfer_results. The WRITE then starts at the end of P's current forward instead of within about 1 ms, which adds up to one P step to D's TTFT under prefill load. WRITE completions also reach the scheduler one step later than on main, because get_transfer_results wakes the writer and drains _push_result_inbox before that pass has polled. Picking up results once per step is fine for completions, but not for this match, because here the writer starts the WRITE itself. Could you keep the timed wait while _push_finished_blocks is non-empty, or post a TTFT comparison against main at a concurrency where P is busy? The GSM8K runs use num_concurrent=1.

nodes.body: _pop_done_transfers now calls xfer_stats.record_transfer on the writer thread. That method makes four separate list appends, while the model thread swaps the data dict in clone_and_reset (get_kv_connector_stats). On main, both ran on the model thread. If the swap lands between two appends, one transfer is split across two intervals. reduce() then fails its assert n == num_successful_transfers (stats.py:137) inside the API server's periodic stats log, which ends that logging task. The window is only a few bytecodes, but every completed WRITE opens it. Return the telemetry with (done, failed) through _push_result_inbox and record it on the model thread, or hold a worker-side lock around record_transfer and clone_and_reset.

inline_comments.body: This also removes main's 1 ms self-poll, which the writer ran while P held finished blocks with no matching PUSH_REG (added with the push connector in #35264). If a PUSH_REG reaches P after the prefill has finished (for example, D queued the request), P now drains it only on its next get_transfer_results. The WRITE then starts at the end of P's current forward instead of within about 1 ms, which adds up to one P step to D's TTFT under prefill load. WRITE completions also reach the scheduler one step later than on main, because get_transfer_results wakes the writer and drains _push_result_inbox before that pass has polled. Picking up results once per step is fine for completions, but not for this match, because here the writer starts the WRITE itself. Could you keep the timed wait while _push_finished_blocks is non-empty, or post a TTFT comparison against main at a concurrency where P is busy? The GSM8K runs use num_concurrent=1.

inline_comments.body: _pop_done_transfers now calls xfer_stats.record_transfer on the writer thread. That method makes four separate list appends, while the model thread swaps the data dict in clone_and_reset (get_kv_connector_stats). On main, both ran on the model thread. If the swap lands between two appends, one transfer is split across two intervals. reduce() then fails its assert n == num_successful_transfers (stats.py:137) inside the API server's periodic stats log, which ends that logging task. The window is only a few bytecodes, but every completed WRITE opens it. Return the telemetry with (done, failed) through _push_result_inbox and record it on the model thread, or hold a worker-side lock around record_transfer and clone_and_reset.

Thanks for the update!

I see your point, yet I'd drop the 1 ms polling. As I understand it, it doesn't solve what you are trying to solve.

Even if the writer polls every ms, the model thread only picks up the results once per engine step. So the thread can poll as much as it wants. It has no effect until the engine finishes its step.

Do you maybe have a profile of the rank that blocked?
I suspect P sends no heartbeats because `heartbeat_by_engine` is only filled on D. And `check_xfer_state` has no blocking wait in NIXL.

@YannikHinteregger you were right about the 1 ms poll. On cebf114 the writer only uses that wait while a PUSH_REG is still unmatched. In-flight writes just wake with the engine step, and check_xfer_state does not hold the lock. The handshake lock only covers the two agent setup calls, and the heartbeat map is copied before it is queued. I also removed the receive override.
